A separate track is the A7 cryptocurrency network: in April the Financial Times wrote of limited evidence of its practical progress on the continent, but in October the Centre for Information Resilience identified numerous technical links with international payment platforms, including the Togo-linked Amani AI. Participants in the A7 network are under British sanctions.

Russian expansion in the gold-mining sector can weaken state control over national resources and channel revenues towards Russian military objectives. This mechanism is already visible in the Central African Republic: according to the US Treasury, the Wagner-linked company Midas, together with mercenaries, obstructed state inspections of the Ndassima mine, while revenues of related companies supported military operations. Against this background, new projects require particular attention. In Mali a gold-processing plant is under construction: 62% of the joint company belongs to the state, 38% to the Russian firm Yadran. Processing of raw materials from other Sahel countries is being considered, which could turn the plant into a regional hub. In Niger, Rosgeologia has so far reported only readiness to sign agreements on hydrocarbon and gold exploration. For Moscow, gold is valuable both as income and as an asset for operations outside ordinary Western banking channels.

Russia's media presence combines open agreements with covert operations that mislead African audiences. Ahead of the summit, TASS signed agreements with media partners in Burundi, Guinea, Cameroon, Mali, Niger, the Seychelles and Tanzania on news exchange, training and reciprocal visits. The network covers both close security partners of Moscow and states with other forms of cooperation. According to RT, TASS also provides its news feeds free of charge to more than 300 African media outlets. This work began long before the current summit and ensures continuous access to newsrooms. In parallel, Graphika and Code for Africa identified a network of likely fabricated journalists and experts promoting Russian interests; researchers have a high level of confidence regarding 38 such individuals.

The recruitment of Africans for the war is a direct human cost that is not offset by trade or diplomatic benefits. In August the Ukrainian Foreign Ministry reported at least 2 982 recruits from 37 African countries and around 486 known deaths. These are incomplete figures from the Ukrainian side, but independent research confirms the mechanism of abuse. Amnesty International has documented deception, coercion and the exploitation of economic hardship that in many cases amount to human trafficking. In Kenya, families are publicly demanding answers and the return of their relatives.

Russian military presence draws African states into Moscow's broader struggle for strategic positions. Russia has long sought a permanent naval presence on the continent, but this remains an unrealized ambition. The project in Port Sudan has been delayed for years. As late as the end of 2025 the Russian ambassador explained the pause by the war; Sudan Tribune, citing its own sources at the time, reported that al-Burhan had assured the Saudi side that plans for a Red Sea base had been frozen. At the same time Russia is expanding access to Libyan airfields, including Maaten al-Sarra near the borders with Chad and Sudan, supporting its operations in the Sahel. The infrastructure already exists, although guaranteed long-term access and a permanent naval base remain unresolved. The harm from previous operations in Libya is concrete: Human Rights Watch established Wagner's involvement in the mining of areas near Tripoli in 2020.

The gap between the Russian offer and the development needs of African countries risks perpetuating their economic vulnerability. The co-chair of the summit, President of Burundi Évariste Ndayishimiye, called on Russian companies to invest in local processing, jobs and skills transfer. For African governments it is important to retain a larger share of the revenues from their own resources. This is precisely where the Russian offer falls short: trade (with a surplus in Russia's favor) is more developed than large-scale productive investment.
Without the development of local production and skills, countries can remain suppliers of raw materials and buyers of finished goods. This suits Moscow but does not help its partners in Africa.

The principal danger of the Russian model is the transformation of vital needs of African societies into dependence, a significant share of whose costs is borne by the African population itself. Moscow entrenches itself through military support, food supplies and, in prospect, electricity. In the three years between summits it has expanded its presence and strengthened ties with a number of African states, gaining influence without large-scale investment in development. The social cost of this model of cooperation can already be assessed: violence against civilians, recruitment by deception, covert information operations and the restriction of state control over resources have all been documented.

第三届“俄罗斯—非洲”峰会将于2026年10月28日至29日在莫斯科举行。

本次峰会的主要政治成果是，尽管其政策给非洲人带来损害，莫斯科仍与非洲保持着广泛联系。据组织方称，已有48个国家确认参加，其中22个国家由国家元首代表。在2023年的上一届峰会上，这类领导人有17位；而在2019年的首届峰会上，则有43位。这表明参与程度有所恢复，克里姆林宫可以将其作为获得国际认可的证据。肯尼亚是一个颇具说明力的例子：上一届峰会由大使代表，而此次代表团由总统Ruto率领，尽管招募肯尼亚人加入俄罗斯军队的问题依然紧迫。

永久性合作框架巩固了俄罗斯的影响力，却无法保证非洲伙伴的承诺会得到兑现。峰会期间，Lavrov与非洲联盟委员会主席签署了一份涵盖2027年至2029年、涉及19个领域的计划，范围从安全、能源到教育。这为各届峰会之间建立了工作渠道，也扩大了莫斯科接触非洲机构的机会。与此同时，俄罗斯外交部早在6月就承认，以往会议产出的宣言多于实际协议。

俄罗斯的军事支持帮助某些政权维持统治，并加深它们对莫斯科的依赖。据FDD评估，自2023年以来，俄罗斯军事存在的地理范围已扩大至至少9个国家。尼日尔说明了这种军事存在如何转化为政治筹码。8月底，部分军队发动哗变期间，俄罗斯军队协助当局镇压了起义。据俄罗斯大使称，尼日尔方面主动请求了援助。

即使俄罗斯的支持无法提供可靠的安全保障，并伴随着针对民众的暴力，其依赖关系仍可能持续存在。今年春天，非洲军团被迫撤出马里北部的基达尔。10月，在俄罗斯支持下，马里军队重新夺回该城，但这一事件也显示了莫斯科能力的局限。Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung专家Ulf Laessing解释称，马里当局之所以维持伙伴关系，是因为缺乏可行的替代方案。与此同时，10月，Human Rights Watch记录了涉及非洲军团俄罗斯雇佣兵的新一轮酷刑迫害平民事件。

尽管俄罗斯自身的行动加剧了粮食不安全，它却正在增加从对非粮食供应中获得的收入。2026年前9个月，莫斯科向非洲交付了价值超过37亿美元的农产品，比一年前增长9%。按金额计算，增幅最大的是肯尼亚；与此同时，该国正敦促解决本国公民在俄罗斯军队中服役的问题。食品供应对买方具有价值，但必须结合俄罗斯对乌克兰战争造成的影响来评估。俄罗斯2023年退出黑海粮食倡议后，联合国秘书长曾警告其对脆弱国家及价格上涨造成的影响。

核能有可能把用电需求变成对俄罗斯的长期依赖。Rosatom推介了浮动核电站，并称正与埃及、多哥、纳米比亚和坦桑尼亚进行高级别谈判。拟议模式是由相关国家购买电力，同时由俄罗斯继续参与维护和燃料供应。这些核电站最长可运行60年，使相关国家对供应方的联系持久而难以替代。目前这些项目仍没有公开确认的合同、议定的融资方案或时间表。已经启动的最大项目是埃及El Dabaa核电站的建设。

俄罗斯支付网络之间不透明的联系，给非洲伙伴带来金融和制裁风险。Putin呼吁扩大银行间联系、开设分支机构，并将俄罗斯的SPFS与泛非支付系统并行使用。通过这种方式，莫斯科寻求将自身的金融工具与非洲基础设施连接起来。

另一条路线是A7加密货币网络：4月，《金融时报》报道称，该网络在非洲大陆的实际进展证据有限；但10月，Centre for Information Resilience发现它与国际支付平台之间存在众多技术联系，其中包括与多哥有关联的Amani AI。A7网络的参与者受到英国制裁。

俄罗斯向黄金开采领域扩张，可能削弱国家对本国资源的控制，并把收入导向俄罗斯的军事目标。这一机制在中非共和国已经显现：据美国财政部称，与Wagner有关联的公司Midas及其雇佣兵妨碍国家检查Ndassima矿山，而相关公司的收入则用于支持军事行动。在这种背景下，新项目尤其值得关注。马里正在建设一座黄金加工厂：合资公司的62%股权归国家，38%归俄罗斯企业Yadran。该厂还在考虑加工其他萨赫勒国家的原材料，这可能使其成为区域枢纽。在尼日尔，Rosgeologia迄今只报告称已准备就碳氢化合物和黄金勘探签署协议。对莫斯科而言，黄金既是收入来源，也是支持其在常规西方银行体系之外开展行动的资产。

俄罗斯在媒体领域的存在，将公开协议与误导非洲受众的秘密行动结合起来。峰会前夕，TASS与布隆迪、几内亚、喀麦隆、马里、尼日尔、塞舌尔和坦桑尼亚的媒体伙伴签署了新闻交换、培训和互访协议。该网络既涵盖莫斯科的密切安全伙伴，也包括采取其他形式合作的国家。据RT报道，TASS还免费向300多家非洲媒体机构提供新闻源。这项工作早在本届峰会之前很久便已开始，并确保新闻编辑部持续获得其内容。与此同时，Graphika和Code for Africa识别出一个由疑似虚构记者和专家构成的网络，专门宣扬俄罗斯利益；研究人员高度确信其中有38名此类人员。

为战争招募非洲人是直接的人力代价，无法被贸易或外交利益抵消。8月，乌克兰外交部报告称，来自37个非洲国家的受征者至少有2 982人，已知死亡人数约为486人。这些是乌克兰方面提供的并不完整的数据，但独立研究证实了相关虐待机制。Amnesty International记录了欺骗、胁迫以及利用经济困境进行剥削的行为，其中许多已构成人口贩运。在肯尼亚，民众家属公开要求给出答案，并要求其亲人归来。

俄罗斯的军事存在把非洲国家卷入莫斯科争夺战略位置的更大角力。俄罗斯长期以来一直寻求在非洲大陆建立永久性海军存在，但这仍是一个尚未实现的愿望。Port Sudan项目已拖延多年。截至2025年底，俄罗斯大使仍以战争为由解释项目暂停；Sudan Tribune当时援引自身消息人士报道称，al-Burhan已向沙特方面保证，在红海设立基地的计划已被冻结。与此同时，俄罗斯正扩大对利比亚机场的使用权，包括靠近乍得和苏丹边界的Maaten al-Sarra，以支持其在萨赫勒地区的行动。相关基础设施已经存在，但长期使用权得到保障和永久海军基地仍未解决。此前在利比亚的行动造成的损害十分具体：Human Rights Watch确认，2020年Wagner曾参与开采的黎波里附近地区。

俄罗斯的提议与非洲国家的发展需求之间的差距，可能使其经济脆弱性长期延续。本届峰会共同主席、布隆迪总统Évariste Ndayishimiye呼吁俄罗斯企业投资当地加工、创造就业并推动技能转让。对非洲政府而言，重要的是让本国资源收入中的更大份额留在本国。俄罗斯的提议恰恰在这一点上存在不足：贸易（且顺差有利于俄罗斯）比大规模生产性投资发展得更为充分。如果没有本地生产和技能的发展，国家就可能继续充当原材料供应者和制成品买家。这适合莫斯科，却无助于其非洲伙伴。

俄罗斯模式的主要危险，在于把非洲社会的基本需求转变为依赖关系，而其中相当一部分成本最终由非洲民众自身承担。莫斯科通过军事支持、粮食供应以及未来的电力供应不断巩固自身地位。在两届峰会之间的3年里，它扩大了自身存在，并加强了与多个非洲国家的关系，在没有大规模发展投资的情况下获得了影响力。这种合作模式的社会代价已经可以得到评估：针对平民的暴力、以欺骗手段招募人员、秘密信息行动，以及国家对资源控制权的削弱，均已得到记录。

俄罗斯的军事存在把非洲国家卷入莫斯科争夺战略位置的更大角力。俄罗斯长期以来一直寻求在非洲大陆建立永久性海军存在，但这仍是一个尚未实现的愿望。Port Sudan项目已拖延多年。截至2025年底，俄罗斯大使仍以战争为由解释项目暂停；Sudan Tribune当时援引自身消息人士报道称，al-Burhan已向沙特方面保证，在红海设立基地的计划已被冻结。与此同时，俄罗斯正扩大对利比亚机场的使用权，包括靠近乍得和苏丹边界的Maaten al-Sarra，以支持其在萨赫勒地区的行动。相关基础设施已经存在，但长期使用权得到保障和永久海军基地仍未解决。此前在利比亚的行动造成的损害十分具体：Human Rights Watch确认，2020年Wagner曾参与开采的黎波里附近地区。

俄罗斯的提议与非洲国家的发展需求之间的差距，可能使其经济脆弱性长期延续。本届峰会共同主席、布隆迪总统Évariste Ndayishimiye呼吁俄罗斯企业投资当地加工、创造就业并推动技能转让。对非洲政府而言，重要的是让本国资源收入中的更大份额留在本国。俄罗斯的提议恰恰在这一点上存在不足：贸易（且顺差有利于俄罗斯）比大规模生产性投资发展得更为充分。如果没有本地生产和技能的发展，国家就可能继续充当原材料供应者和制成品买家。这适合莫斯科，却无助于其非洲伙伴。

俄罗斯模式的主要危险，在于把非洲社会的基本需求转变为依赖关系，而其中相当一部分成本最终由非洲民众自身承担。莫斯科通过军事支持、粮食供应以及未来的电力供应不断巩固自身地位。在两届峰会之间的3年里，它扩大了自身存在，并加强了与多个非洲国家的关系，在没有大规模发展投资的情况下获得了影响力。这种合作模式的社会代价已经可以得到评估：针对平民的暴力、以欺骗手段招募人员、秘密信息行动，以及国家对资源控制权的削弱，均已得到记录。

#RadioMoskva

3rd Africa Russian summit

Putin is having fun as delegations from 48 of Africa's 54 countries, 22 led by heads of state, are in Moscow for the third Russia-Africa summit, where Putin is selling Russia as Africa's anti-colonial partner.

He is on a roll to an eager audience, giving rousing speeches on his favourite topic: the world has been ruled by a bunch of neo-colonist imperialists that are just interested in bleeding the developing world of its human capital wealth to enrich themselves and the workers of the Global South should unite!

This is the third time for the summit, following the first one in Sochi in 2019 and it has been a huge success. The message resonates as much of the message is true. A study we reported found that the West exports some 80% of its manufacturing needs to the developing world, to sweat shops in places like Myanmar, where the “multinationals” pay pennies to have our phones and jeans made. That really does export the human capital wealth from these countries and enrich us in the developed world as a iPhone costs $1,000 and not the $5,000 it would cost if an American made it. That’s $4,000 of cash you can spend on something else. This system was politely known as “globalization” until recently but, as Putin keeps pushing, it can also be called neo-colonialism. At least, the Africans see it that way.

Ironically, this system is exactly what US President Donald Trump is complaining about and the reason for his Liberation Day tariffs – to bring “good manufacturing jobs back home.”

But this is beyond stupid, as it takes no account of the income delta: we did a back of the envelope calculation of the unit cost of making a widget in the EU, US and China using one kilo of metal, 100kWh of power and an hour of average labour: it costs around $25 in the developed world and only $7 in China – and China already has some of the more expensive labour costs in the EMs.

You can’t compete with this, no matter how high you build your trade protectionist walls. As we have been arguing all year, we are now in a post-Pax Americana world as the “emerging markets” have emerged. They should be renamed something like the “dynamic markets” (that is not really catchy enough, eh?) as they still have a lot of problems and the wage delta remains, but the China story shows very clearly that they are catching up in a lot of sectors and even overtaking the DMs in things like Greentech.

But not Africa. That really is still an emerging market story. The per capita incomes in Africa are still a fraction of even Russia’s income. It’s the last really big EM catch up story that has yet to unwind. And Russia is promising to help.

Russia was in the first wave. I was in the room at Putin’s first ever state of the nation speech in 2000 when he put demographics at the top of the agenda – it’s still top of the list – but he his top economic agenda item was to “catch up with Portugal.”

26 years later Russia has overtaken not only Portugal, but everyone else, except the US on a ppp basis.

This process is going in waves. Central Europe caught up with the DMs really fast after the EU accession wave in 2003. China has seen its growth accelerate for about a decade and is now slowing and maturing. Central Asia is only coming to its critical mass now, where Uzbekistan has been putting in 6% growth for a decade but recently started to accelerate and growth is now around 8% with another decade of fast growth ahead. Latin America is doing the same and the Brazilian economy in particular has been transformed and now accounts for a third of GDP of the whole continent by itself.

Africa is right at the start of the process, with a few hot spots like Nigeria. Sub-Saharan African growth averaged 4.5% in both 2026 and 2027 with East Africa growing the fastest at 6.5% projected for this year.

It usually starts with FDI into light manufacturing, but most of Africa is still at the exporting-raw-materials stage. It’s an issue of low wages vs productivity. The Balkans is currently booming as productivity has risen to the point where the combination of the two makes it more profitable than investing in Central Europe. In Africa the wages are essentially zero, but so is the productivity.

In this context, listening to Putin’s speeches today and yesterday and he is pushing all of Africa’s buttons. He is not only promising to provide grain – a top necessity for many countries – but yesterday he also promised to invest into African pharmaceutical sector, and today promised to build factories and move some Russian production to Africa. He also mentioned that the number of African students studying in Russia has doubled in the last year and Rosatom was holding talks on building half a dozen floating nuclear power stations in Africa. These are all productivity multipliers and the assembled presidents are creaming themselves over the prospects as Russia usually finances these sorts of investments itself – for the Africans they are essentially free (in the short-term but come with strategic dependencies…).

The neo-colonial troupe is the Xmas wrapping paper this is all bundled into. Another story earlier this month that went by largely unnoticed was a Russia sponsored UN motion to condemn sanctions as neo-colonial, which was universally approved by the Global South and university condemned by the EU and US. The Kremlin completely outplayed the West with that one. France was booted out of Niger in 2023 because it was paying a fraction for a kilo for uranium, an estimated €68/kg, when the market price was closer to €200. Macron regularly gets booed when he tours in francophone Africa – he simply doesn’t get it.

All this is important as its part of Putin’s big bet on the Global South Century. He must have been fully aware of what would happen when he marched into Ukraine – a permeant break with the West and the end of his dream of a single market “from Lisbon to Vladivostok” which most of his foreign policy was built around. Swapping Germany for Sahel may not look like such a great idea, but when you add in Latam, SE Asia and particularly China, it starts to get more appealing: Putin pointed out that just the BRICS generated 40% of global GDP last year. And Africa will eventually be a big catch as it shares many features with Russia: a large land mass, a large population, and a cornucopia of raw materials. Putin’s plan is clearly to accelerate the catch up, and the Africans are lovin’ it.

Russia is so well received as it never tried to colonise Africa and indeed, during the Cold War the communist USSR supported the independence movements against their colonial overlords. And since then Russia remains the destination of choice for a quality higher education. You’d be surprised at how many of the African delegates in Moscow today speak fluent Russian from their university days. For example, presidents João Lourenço of Angola and John Dramani Mahama of Ghana both studied in Moscow.

France was booted out of Niger in 2023 because it was paying a fraction for a kilo for uranium, an estimated €68/kg, when the market price was closer to €200. Macron regularly gets booed when he tours in francophone Africa – he simply doesn’t get it.

All this is important as its part of Putin’s big bet on the Global South Century. He must have been fully aware of what would happen when he marched into Ukraine – a permeant break with the West and the end of his dream of a single market “from Lisbon to Vladivostok” which most of his foreign policy was built around. Swapping Germany for Sahel may not look like such a great idea, but when you add in Latam, SE Asia and particularly China, it starts to get more appealing: Putin pointed out that just the BRICS generated 40% of global GDP last year. And Africa will eventually be a big catch as it shares many features with Russia: a large land mass, a large population, and a cornucopia of raw materials. Putin’s plan is clearly to accelerate the catch up, and the Africans are lovin’ it.

Russia is so well received as it never tried to colonise Africa and indeed, during the Cold War the communist USSR supported the independence movements against their colonial overlords. And since then Russia remains the destination of choice for a quality higher education. You’d be surprised at how many of the African delegates in Moscow today speak fluent Russian from their university days. For example, presidents João Lourenço of Angola and John Dramani Mahama of Ghana both studied in Moscow.

俄罗斯广播电台

第三届非洲-俄罗斯峰会

普京正与来自非洲54国中48国的代表团共同欢庆，其中22国由国家元首率领，这些代表团齐聚莫斯科参加第三届俄罗斯-非洲峰会，普京在会上将俄罗斯定位为非洲的反殖民伙伴。

他在一群热切的听众面前侃侃而谈，就自己最喜欢的话题发表激动人心的演讲：世界一直被一群新殖民帝国主义者统治，他们只对榨取发展中国家的人力资本财富来 enriching 自己感兴趣，全球南方国家的劳动者应该团结起来！

这是该峰会第三次举办，上一次于2019年在索契举行，此次峰会取得巨大成功。其传递的信息引起广泛共鸣，因为其中很多内容是真实的。我们此前报道的一项研究发现，西方将其制造需求的约80%出口到发展中国家，转移到像缅甸那样的血汗工厂，在那里“跨国公司”只支付几分钱就让当地工人生产我们的手机和牛仔裤。这确实把这些国家的人力资本财富输出出去，并让我们发达国家变得更加富有，因为一部iPhone售价1000美元，而不是如果由美国工人制造可能需要的5000美元。这意味着你可以把省下的4000美元用于其他消费。这种体系直到最近还被礼貌地称为“全球化”，但正如普京不断指出的那样，它也可以被称为新殖民主义。至少，非洲人就是这样看待它的。

具有讽刺意味的是，这种体系正是美国总统唐纳德·特朗普所抱怨的内容，也是他实施解放日关税的原因——目的是把“良好的制造业就业机会带回国内”。

但这样做极其愚蠢，因为它完全没有考虑收入差距：我们做过一个粗略计算，用1公斤金属、10万瓦时电力和1小时平均劳动力在欧盟、美国和中国制造一个小部件的单位成本：在发达国家大约需要25美元，而在中国只需7美元——中国在新兴市场中已经属于劳动力成本较高的国家之一。

无论你把贸易保护主义壁垒筑得多高，都无法与此竞争。正如我们全年一直主张的那样，我们现在正处于后美国治世世界，因为“新兴市场”已经崛起。它们或许应该被重新命名为“动态市场”（这个名字确实不够吸引人，对吧？），因为它们仍存在许多问题且工资差距依然存在，但中国的故事清楚表明，它们正在许多领域迎头赶上，甚至在绿色科技等领域超越发达市场。

但非洲并非如此。非洲确实仍是一个新兴市场故事。非洲的人均收入甚至只是俄罗斯收入的一小部分。这是最后一个尚未展开的真正大型新兴市场追赶故事。而俄罗斯承诺提供帮助。

俄罗斯处于第一波。我曾在2000年亲临现场，听取普京首次国情咨文演讲，当时他把人口问题置于议程首位——至今仍是首要问题——但他当时最重要的经济议程是“赶上葡萄牙”。

26年后，俄罗斯不仅超过了葡萄牙，而且按购买力平价计算还超过了除美国以外的所有其他国家。

这一进程是分阶段推进的。中欧在2003年加入欧盟浪潮后迅速赶上发达市场。中国经济增长加速了大约十年，现在正在放缓并走向成熟。中亚现在才达到关键规模，乌兹别克斯坦十年来一直保持6%的增长，但最近开始加速，目前增长率约为8%，未来十年仍将保持快速增长。拉丁美洲也在经历同样的过程，特别是巴西经济已发生转变，现在独自占整个大陆国内生产总值的三分之一。

非洲正处于这一进程的起点，只有少数热点地区如尼日利亚。撒哈拉以南非洲在2026年和2027年经济增长均平均达到4.5%，东非今年预计增长最快，达到6.5%。

这一进程通常始于外国直接投资进入轻制造业，但非洲大部分地区仍处于出口原材料阶段。这是一个低工资与生产率之间的问题。巴尔干地区目前正在蓬勃发展，因为那里的生产率已提高到使两者结合比投资中欧更有利可图的程度。在非洲，工资基本上为零，但生产率同样为零。

在这种背景下，听取普京今天和昨天的演讲，他正在按下非洲的所有按钮。他不仅承诺提供粮食——这是许多国家的首要必需品——而且昨天他还承诺投资非洲制药业，今天又承诺在非洲建厂并将部分俄罗斯生产转移到非洲。他还提到，去年在俄罗斯学习的非洲学生人数翻了一番，俄罗斯国家原子能公司正在就为非洲建造六座浮动核电站进行谈判。这些都是生产率倍增器，与会的总统们对这些前景兴奋不已，因为俄罗斯通常会自己为这类投资提供资金——对非洲人来说，这些投资基本上是免费的（短期内如此，但会带来战略依赖……）。

新殖民主义论调就是包裹这一切的圣诞包装纸。本月早些时候还有一个基本上未被注意到的故事，即俄罗斯赞助的一项联合国决议，谴责制裁是新殖民主义行为，该决议得到全球南方的普遍支持，却遭到欧盟和美国的强烈谴责。克里姆林宫在这件事上完全胜过了西方。法国2023年被尼日尔驱逐，因为它以远低于市场价的价格购买铀，每公斤仅支付约68欧元，而当时市场价格接近200欧元。马克龙在法语非洲国家巡访时经常遭到嘘声——他根本不明白这一点。

所有这些都很重要，因为这是普京对全球南方世纪所下的大赌注的一部分。他一定完全清楚，当他进军乌克兰时会发生什么——与西方永久决裂，并终结他建立“从里斯本到符拉迪沃斯托克”单一市场的梦想，而他的大部分外交政策正是围绕这一梦想构建的。用萨赫勒国家联盟取代德国看起来可能不是一个好主意，但当你加上拉美、东南亚特别是中国时，它就开始变得更有吸引力：普京指出，仅金砖国家去年就贡献了全球国内生产总值的40%。非洲最终将成为一大收获，因为它与俄罗斯有许多共同特征：广阔的土地、庞大的人口以及丰富的原材料。普京的计划显然是加速这一追赶进程，而非洲人对此非常喜爱。

俄罗斯受到如此欢迎，是因为它从未试图殖民非洲，而且确实，在冷战期间，共产主义的苏联支持了反对殖民宗主国的独立运动。从那以后，俄罗斯仍然是接受高质量高等教育的首选目的地。你可能会惊讶于今天在莫斯科的非洲代表中有多少人能说流利的俄语，这得益于他们大学时代的学习。例如，安哥拉总统若昂·洛伦索和加纳总统约翰·德拉马尼·马哈马都曾在莫斯科学习。

Hon. Agbodza Explores Stronger Ghana-China Partnership in Road Infrastructure Development

The Minister of Roads and Highways, Hon. Kwame Governs Agbodza, has reaffirmed Government’s commitment to strengthen bilateral relations between Ghana and China while exploring opportunities for further collaboration in road infrastructure development. 

He made this known when a joint delegation from the Jiangxi Provincial State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission (Jiangxi Provincial SASAC) and China Jiangxi International Economic and Technical Cooperation Company Ltd. paid a courtesy call on him to discuss existing relations and prospects for future partnerships with the Ministry.

Hon. Agbodza underscored government’s commitment to maintaining a mutually beneficial relationship between the two countries. “President Mahama has arguably made the largest scale of infrastructure investment within the road sector under the Big Push Programme and Chinese companies are participating significantly. The relationship between Ghana and China is very important to us and we promise to do what we can to sustain it,” he said. 

He noted that cooperation with international institutions and development partners remains important in mobilising investment, technical expertise and other resources to support the country’s road infrastructure priorities.

Hon. Agbodza Explores Stronger Ghana-China Partnership in Road Infrastructure Development

The Minister of Roads and Highways, Hon. Kwame Governs Agbodza, has reaffirmed Government’s commitment to strengthen bilateral relations between Ghana and China while exploring opportunities for further collaboration in road infrastructure development. 

He made this known when a joint delegation from the Jiangxi Provincial State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission (Jiangxi Provincial SASAC) and China Jiangxi International Economic and Technical Cooperation Company Ltd. paid a courtesy call on him to discuss existing relations and prospects for future partnerships with the Ministry.

Hon. Agbodza underscored government’s commitment to maintaining a mutually beneficial relationship between the two countries. “President Mahama has arguably made the largest scale of infrastructure investment within the road sector under the Big Push Programme and Chinese companies are participating significantly. The relationship between Ghana and China is very important to us and we promise to do what we can to sustain it,” he said. 

He noted that cooperation with international institutions and development partners remains important in mobilising investment, technical expertise and other resources to support the country’s road infrastructure priorities.

The delegation was led by Mr. Xiao Yun, Director-General of Jiangxi Provincial SASAC, together with Mr. Xu Zhenghua, Vice President of CJIC.

https://x.com/tribunephl/status/21156445.snippet:
CHINA OWNS 40% OF THE COMPANY RUNNING OUR POWER GRID

The Philippine government owns the country's electricity transmission infrastructure, but the private company operating it, the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines (#NGCP), is 40 percent owned by China's state-owned State Grid Corporation.

That means the Chinese government holds a substantial stake in the company responsible for transmitting electricity across the Philippines, even as tensions between Manila and Beijing persist in the West Philippine Sea.

NGCP maintains that Filipino engineers operate the grid, and there is no established evidence that China possesses a secret mechanism to shut it down.

But the ownership arrangement raises a national security question: Should a foreign government with which the Philippines has an ongoing territorial dispute own part of the company operating its electricity transmission network?

https://x.com/tribunephl/status/21156445.snippet_zh:
运营我国电网的公司40%股权归中国所有

菲律宾政府拥有该国的输电基础设施，但负责运营这些设施的私营公司菲律宾国家电网公司（#NGCP）有40%的股权由中国国有国家电网公司持有。

这意味着，在马尼拉与北京于西菲律宾海持续紧张对峙之际，中国政府仍持有这家负责向菲律宾各地输电的公司相当可观的所有权权益。

NGCP坚持表示，菲律宾工程师负责电网运营，而且没有确凿证据表明中国掌握着秘密手段，可以关闭该电网。

但这种股权安排提出了一个国家安全问题：菲律宾与一个存在持续领土争端的国家，该国政府是否应持有负责运营菲律宾输电网络之公司的部分股权？

From Stability to Opportunity: Reflections on Nigeria’s Engagement with Asia

In Beijing, Central Bank of Nigeria @cenbank Governor Olayemi Cardoso (@olayemicardoso1) led discussions across two major forums aimed at expanding Nigeria’s economic and financial ties with China.

The first gathering brought together business executives, financial experts and industry stakeholders operating along the Nigeria–China trade corridor. Conversations centred on payment systems, foreign exchange, trade financing and the challenges businesses face when conducting cross-border transactions.

The second forum, organised in collaboration with ICBC, focused on investment opportunities within Nigeria’s financial markets. Institutional investors, development finance organisations and other market participants examined ways to encourage investment and create a more supportive environment for capital inflows.

Cardoso also highlighted the importance of improving remittance services for Nigerians living abroad. The CBN’s focus includes making international transfers more affordable, accessible and efficient, while strengthening the financial links between the diaspora and Nigeria’s domestic economy.

在北京，尼日利亚中央银行行长奥拉耶米·卡多索（@olayemicardoso1）主持了两场重要论坛的讨论，旨在扩大尼日利亚与中国的经济和金融联系。

https://x.com/africaishome2/status/21154.title: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov has described the reported diesel supply agreement between Russia and the United States as a purely c
https://x.com/africaishome2/status/21154.snippet:
Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov has described the reported diesel supply agreement between Russia and the United States as a purely commercial arrangement, insisting that it carries no additional political or security conditions. Speaking in Moscow on October 27, 2026, Lavrov said the agreement reflects a pragmatic approach by both countries to protect their economic interests and contribute to the stability of global energy markets. He stressed that Washington had not conditioned its purchase of Russian diesel on Moscow taking specific political or security actions, including measures related to the Strait of Hormuz. His comments follow discussions between US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin on expanding Russian fuel supplies to the American and international markets. The agreement has attracted attention because it represents an area of economic cooperation between the two countries despite continuing disagreements over the war in Ukraine and other geopolitical issues.

The diesel arrangement could have broader implications for international energy trade, particularly as countries seek additional fuel supplies amid concerns about prices and market stability. Russia has indicated its readiness to supply more diesel, with officials previously outlining plans for successive shipments and suggesting that cooperation could extend to other areas, including fertilisers and energy projects. However, the agreement has also drawn criticism from Ukraine and some European officials, who argue that renewed Russian energy sales could provide Moscow with additional revenue while the war continues. Lavrov, meanwhile, criticised European involvement in diplomatic negotiations, arguing that European governments had yet to demonstrate a substantially different approach. His remarks also included accusations that Western countries were supporting Ukrainian military personnel involved in sabotage in the Sahel region of Africa; these claims were presented by Lavrov and were not independently established in the report.
World Business News.

https://x.com/africaishome2/status/21154.title_zh: 俄罗斯外长谢尔盖·拉夫罗夫将据报道的俄罗斯与美国柴油供应协议描述为纯粹的……
https://x.com/africaishome2/status/21154.snippet_zh:
俄罗斯外交部长谢尔盖·拉夫罗夫将据报道达成的俄美柴油供应协议描述为一项纯粹的商业安排，并坚称其中不包含任何附加的政治或安全条件。拉夫罗夫于2026年10月27日在莫斯科表示，该协议体现了两国保护自身经济利益、推动全球能源市场稳定的务实态度。他强调，华盛顿并未将购买俄罗斯柴油与莫斯科采取特定政治或安全行动挂钩，包括采取与霍尔木兹海峡有关的措施。此前，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京曾讨论扩大俄罗斯燃料对美国及国际市场的供应。上述协议引起关注，是因为尽管两国在乌克兰战争及其他地缘政治问题上仍存在分歧，但经济合作仍能在这些领域之外取得进展。

这项柴油供应安排可能对国际能源贸易产生更广泛的影响，尤其是在各国因担忧价格和市场稳定而寻求额外燃料供应之际。俄罗斯已表示愿意增加柴油供应，官员此前还概述了分批装运的计划，并暗示合作可能扩展至其他领域，包括化肥和能源项目。然而，该协议也遭到乌克兰及一些欧洲官员的批评。他们认为，战争仍在持续之际，恢复俄罗斯能源销售可能为莫斯科带来额外收入。与此同时，拉夫罗夫批评欧洲参与外交谈判，称欧洲政府迄今尚未展现出实质性不同的做法。他的言论还指责西方国家支持在非洲萨赫勒地区从事破坏活动的乌克兰军方人员；报道称，这些指控由拉夫罗夫提出，但未得到独立证实。

《世界商业新闻》。

https://x.com/amborin/status/21154911112.title: "Russia can technologically help the US build an LNG plant in Alaska...the Polar LNG project worth $25 billion" "What does Russia need from
https://x.com/amborin/status/21154911112.snippet:
"Russia can technologically help the US build an LNG plant in Alaska...the Polar LNG project worth $25 billion"

"What does Russia need from the US in the Arctic? "two things...first is the market, second is iron. The lifting of sanctions on the Arctic LNG-2 and its LNG carriers will bring back buyers from Japan, India, Southeast Asia and remove the discount that is now being taken away by the only client - China"

"A diesel deal with the United States, an opportunity to expand the supply of Russian fertilizers, and now Russia is offering to work together in the Arctic. How could the Arctic unite Russia and the United States, and what can Moscow offer Washington in return for lifting sanctions on Russian gas?

Russia is working on the possibility of joint work with the United States in the Arctic, Russian President Vladimir Putin said.

"In the Arctic, which I mentioned, we are actively working with many countries of the world and are interested in working together. Quite recently, European partners worked with us in our fields. Now we are working on the possibility of joint work with American partners," Putin said at the summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF).

What kind of joint work with the United States can Russia have?

We are talking about LNG projects. Indeed, after 2022, due to sanctions against Russia, European companies withdrew from participating in gas projects with Russia - in Yamal LNG and Arctic LNG-2. However, cooperation with Chinese companies has reached a new level, says Igor Yushkov, an expert at the National Energy Security Fund (NEF) and the Financial University under the Government of the Russian Federation. There are two Chinese shareholders in the Arctic LNG 2 - CNPC and CNOOC, which were initially afraid of US sanctions against the project and froze their participation. However, Beijing did not change its policy, just the Chinese companies CNPC and CNOOC did not risk access to the dollar, says Mikhail Vakilyan, an expert at the Institute for the Development of Fuel and Energy Technologies.

But after a year and a half, everything changed. In the second half of 2025, China began buying gas from the sanctioned Arctic LNG-2 plant, allocating an entire terminal for the project, and this year opened a second terminal only for Russian LNG. China has even resumed the delivery of modules for the completion of the third stage of the Arctic LNG-2, although earlier deliveries were suspended.

What does Russia need from the United States in the Arctic? "Russia needs two things. The first is the market, the second is iron. The lifting of sanctions on the Arctic LNG-2 and its LNG carriers will bring back buyers from Japan, India, Southeast Asia and remove the discount that is now being taken away by the only client - China. As for iron, the liquefaction compressors at Yamal LNG and Arctic LNG-2 drive the turbines of Baker Hughes, and this is an American company. Service, spare parts and modernization of these cars run into American export bans," says Vakilyan.

"Here is the same scheme as with the diesel deal. We offer the United States mutually beneficial projects and cooperation in the economy in general in exchange for easing anti-Russian sanctions and putting pressure on Ukraine. We show that this cooperation can be very multifaceted and in different areas: diesel, fertilizers, LNG, and so on,"
says the expert of the National Energy Security Fund and the Financial University under the Government of the Russian Federation.

What can Russia offer the United States in the field of LNG in exchange for the lifting of sanctions? Russia can technologically help the United States build an LNG plant in Alaska. We are talking about the Polar LNG project worth $25 billion.

"Novatek has a technological solution for the LNG project in Alaska, which it applied to the Arctic LNG 2. These are reinforced concrete platforms on which liquefaction equipment is poured - and this is, in fact, an LNG plant. Novatek has already built two such platforms with equipment, and has built a center for the construction of large-capacity offshore structures in Belokamenka. The problem is that both this center and the Arctic LNG-2 plant itself fell under US sanctions. Therefore, we can build such a plant in Alaska in exchange for the lifting of sanctions at least from the center for the construction of large-capacity platforms," Yushkov says.

According to him, Russia can pour a platform in this center, build the LNG plant itself on it and only then drive it to Alaska. This is a simpler solution, because it is expensive to build something in the Arctic itself, and creates restrictions on time and the possibility of importing equipment, etc.

"It is not a fact that this story will come to fruition, because there are many sanctions problems and questions about the economics of the project, but nevertheless, the Americans are interested in our technologies for Alaska, and Russia uses and says that it can do it,"
says Yushkov. However, we should not forget that Russia is the main competitor of the United States in terms of gas, and in recent years, the American leadership has consistently squeezed Russian gas out of the European market, the expert adds. And helping LNG from the United States to occupy the market share that the Russian Federation has lost is not a good idea.

However, in addition to the Arctic LNG 2, there is another Russian project that could benefit from cooperation with the United States. This is Yamal LNG, which is not affected by US sanctions. However, the problem is different. From January 1, 2027, the EU bans the supply of any Russian LNG. "In the first half of the year, Europe took almost all of the plant's products - 9.89 million tons. In two months, these volumes need a new route and a new buyer – and an American trader looks natural in this place," says Vakilyan."

-Vzglyad

普京在天然气出口国论坛峰会上说：“在我刚才提到的北极地区，我们正积极与世界上许多国家开展合作，也希望携手合作。就在不久前，欧洲伙伴还曾在我们的油气田与我们合作。现在，我们正在研究与美国伙伴开展合作的可能性。”

俄罗斯可以在哪些方面与美国开展合作？

这涉及液化天然气项目。确实，2022年以后，由于对俄罗斯实施制裁，欧洲企业退出了参与俄罗斯天然气项目，包括Yamal LNG和Arctic LNG-2。然而，俄罗斯联邦政府下属国家能源安全基金和金融大学的专家伊戈尔·尤什科夫表示，与中国企业的合作已经提升到新的水平。Arctic LNG 2有两名中国股东，即CNPC和CNOOC。两家公司最初担心美国会制裁该项目，因而暂停参与。不过，北京并未改变政策，只是中国公司CNPC和CNOOC不愿冒着使用美元结算的风险。燃料与能源技术发展研究所专家米哈伊尔·瓦基利扬如是说。

但一年半后，情况发生了变化。2025年下半年，中国开始从受制裁的Arctic LNG-2工厂采购天然气，为该项目划拨了一整座码头，今年又启用了一座专门接收俄罗斯液化天然气的码头。中国甚至恢复了为Arctic LNG-2第三阶段完工所需模块的交付，而此前这些交付已暂停。

俄罗斯在北极地区需要美国提供什么？瓦基利扬说：“俄罗斯需要两样东西。第一是市场，第二是钢铁。取消对Arctic LNG-2及其液化天然气运输船的制裁，将让日本、印度和东南亚的买家回归，并消除目前唯一客户——中国所获得的折扣。至于钢铁，Yamal LNG和Arctic LNG-2的液化压缩机会驱动Baker Hughes的涡轮机，而Baker Hughes是一家美国公司。这些设施的维护、备件供应和现代化改造都受到美国出口禁令的限制。”

“这与柴油协议采用的是同一套模式。我们向美国提供互利项目以及整体经济合作，以换取放松对俄制裁，并向乌克兰施压。我们表明，这种合作可以非常广泛，涵盖不同领域，包括柴油、化肥和液化天然气等。”——俄罗斯联邦政府下属国家能源安全基金和金融大学的专家

作为解除制裁的回报，俄罗斯可以在液化天然气领域向美国提供什么？俄罗斯可以在技术上帮助美国在阿拉斯加建造液化天然气工厂。这指的是价值250亿美元的极地LNG项目。

尤什科夫说：“Novatek拥有适用于阿拉斯加液化天然气项目的技术方案，并已将这套方案用于Arctic LNG 2。这是在钢筋混凝土平台上浇筑液化设备，而平台本身就是一座液化天然气工厂。Novatek已经建造了两座配有设备的此类平台，还在别洛卡缅卡建造了一座大型海上结构物建造中心。问题在于，这座建造中心和Arctic LNG-2工厂本身都受到美国制裁。因此，至少只要取消对大型平台建造中心的制裁，我们就可以在阿拉斯加建造这样一座工厂。”

据他介绍，俄罗斯可以在该建造中心浇筑平台，在平台上建成液化天然气工厂，之后再将其运往阿拉斯加。这是一种更简单的方案，因为在北极地区直接建造设施成本高昂，还会受到工期以及进口设备可能性等方面的限制。

尤什科夫说：“这件事最终能否实现尚无定论，因为其中涉及许多制裁问题和项目经济性问题。尽管如此，美国人对我们用于阿拉斯加的技术感兴趣，而俄罗斯也能做到，并表示自己有能力完成。”不过，这位专家补充称，俄罗斯在天然气领域是美国的主要竞争对手。近年来，美国领导层一直设法将俄罗斯天然气挤出欧洲市场。帮助美国液化天然气重新占据俄罗斯联邦失去的市场份额并不是好主意。

然而，除了Arctic LNG 2之外，还有另一个可能从与美国合作中获益的俄罗斯项目，即不受美国制裁影响的Yamal LNG。不过，它面临的是另一个问题。自2027年1月1日起，欧盟将禁止供应任何俄罗斯液化天然气。瓦基利扬说：“今年上半年，欧洲采购了该工厂几乎全部产品，约为989万吨。两个月内，这些货量就需要寻找新的运输路线和新的买家，而美国贸易商显然是合适的选择。”

——《观察》

https://x.com/thetect0nic/status/2115490.snippet:
🇷🇺 Putin hosts 22 African heads of state in Moscow and tells them the West wants to push Africa "back into debt bondage," as Amnesty presses leaders over Africans recruited to fight in Ukraine

Vladimir Putin opened the third Russia-Africa summit in Moscow on Wednesday with a pitch aimed squarely at Washington and Brussels. Delegations from 48 African countries are attending, 22 of them led by heads of state, according to Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov. That is up from 17 heads of state in 2023, though well short of the 43 who came to Sochi in 2019. Kenya's William Ruto, Egypt's Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, Ethiopia's Abiy Ahmed, Rwanda's Paul Kagame and Sudan's army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan are among those listed, along with the Sahel juntas that have swapped French troops for Russian ones.

"The multipolar world is truly becoming a reality, and this trend is objective and irreversible," Putin told the plenary session, according to the Kremlin transcript. He accused unnamed Western countries of tariff wars, "illegitimate sanctions" and "active attempts" to drive Africans "back into debt bondage." He offered grain, fertilizer, nuclear power, hydropower and digital government systems, said Russia has "two of our own large language models" it is ready to share, and set a target of doubling Russia-Africa trade, which he put at over $27 billion last year, to more than $50 billion. He said Russia shipped 13 million tonnes of farm products to Africa in the first nine months of 2026. Leaders are due to adopt an action plan for 2027 to 2029 on Thursday.

The numbers carry a caveat. Al Jazeera notes Russia's trade with Africa is concentrated in a few countries and dwarfed by China's and the EU's, and that Moscow's real growth has been in security: Russian missions or troops now operate in at least nine African countries, according to the consultancy African Security Analysis. There is also a cost Putin did not mention. Amnesty International used the run-up to urge leaders to demand an end to what it calls deceptive and coercive recruitment of Africans to fight for Russia in Ukraine, an issue that has already strained ties with Kenya.

For Americans, the guest list is the point. Kenya is a major non-NATO ally of the United States, and Egypt is one of its largest aid recipients. Both sent their leaders to Moscow during a war Washington is trying to end on terms Russia keeps rejecting.

https://x.com/thetect0nic/status/2115490.snippet_zh:
🇷🇺 普京在莫斯科接待22位非洲国家元首，并称西方想让非洲“重新陷入债务奴役”；与此同时，Amnesty敦促各国领导人关注被招募赴乌克兰作战的非洲人问题

周三，弗拉基米尔·普京在莫斯科主持第三届俄罗斯—非洲峰会，开场讲话明确针对华盛顿和布鲁塞尔。据克里姆林宫助理尤里·乌沙科夫介绍，来自48个非洲国家的代表团与会，其中22个由国家元首率领。2023年出席的国家元首有17位，远少于2019年前往索契的43位。名单中包括肯尼亚总统威廉·鲁托、埃及总统阿卜杜勒·法塔赫·塞西、埃塞俄比亚总理阿比·艾哈迈德、卢旺达总统保罗·卡加梅和苏丹军队领导人阿卜杜勒·法塔赫·布尔汉，以及已用俄军取代法军的萨赫勒军政权代表。

据克里姆林宫会议记录，普京对全体会议表示：“多极世界正在真正成为现实，这一趋势具有客观性且不可逆转。”他指控一些未点名的西方国家发起关税战、实施“非法制裁”，并“积极企图”迫使非洲人“重新陷入债务奴役”。他提出提供粮食、化肥、核能、水电和数字政府系统，称俄罗斯拥有“两个我们自主研发的大型语言模型”，愿意分享，并提出将俄非贸易额翻倍的目标。普京表示，俄非贸易额去年超过$27 billion，而其目标是将其提高至$50 billion以上。他说，2026年前9个月，俄罗斯向非洲运送了1300万吨农产品。各国领导人预计于周四通过2027年至2029年行动计划。

这些数字背后存在一个问题。半岛电视台指出，俄罗斯与非洲的贸易集中在少数几个国家，规模远小于中国和欧盟；据咨询机构African Security Analysis称，莫斯科真正实现增长的是安全领域：俄罗斯的使团或军队目前已在至少9个非洲国家开展行动。普京还提到了一项未被提及的代价。Amnesty International利用峰会前夕的时机，敦促各国领导人要求终止其所称的欺骗性和强制性招募非洲人赴乌克兰为俄罗斯作战。此事已经导致肯尼亚与俄罗斯关系紧张。

对美国人而言，宾客名单才是关键。肯尼亚是美国重要的非北约盟国，埃及则是美国最大的援助接受国之一。在华盛顿试图结束乌克兰战争、并按照俄罗斯持续拒绝的条件达成解决方案之际，两国均派出领导人赴莫斯科。

这些数字背后存在一个问题。半岛电视台指出，俄罗斯与非洲的贸易集中在少数几个国家，规模远小于中国和欧盟；据咨询机构African Security Analysis称，莫斯科真正实现增长的是安全领域：俄罗斯的使团或军队目前已在至少9个非洲国家开展行动。普京还提到了一项未被提及的代价。Amnesty International利用峰会前夕的时机，敦促各国领导人要求终止其所称的欺骗性和强制性招募非洲人赴乌克兰为俄罗斯作战。此事已经导致肯尼亚与俄罗斯关系紧张。

对美国人而言，宾客名单才是关键。肯尼亚是美国重要的非北约盟国，埃及则是美国最大的援助接受国之一。在华盛顿试图结束乌克兰战争、并按照俄罗斯持续拒绝的条件达成解决方案之际，两国均派出领导人赴莫斯科。
